ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First, according to the sum of the interior angles of a triangle, find the third angle: B = 180° - 30° - 105° = 45°. It is known that side a is opposite angle A, and side b is opposite angle B; apply the sine rule a/sinA = b/sinB. Substitute a/sin30° = 4/sin45°, so a = 4·sin30°/sin45° = 4·(1/2)/(√2/2) = 2√2.

method.method_draft: Use the sine rule directly. Read from the problem that in triangle ABC, angle A = 30°, angle C = 105°, and side b = 4. First compute the remaining angle B = 180° - 30° - 105° = 45°. Using the standard notation that side a is opposite angle A and side b is opposite angle B, apply a/sin A = b/sin B. Thus a = 4·sin30°/sin45° = 4·(1/2)/(√2/2) = 2√2.

method.method_draft: Use an altitude construction and special right triangles. Read that A = 30°, C = 105°, b = AC = 4, and side a = BC is required. Compute B = 45°. Drop perpendicular CD from C to AB. In right triangle ACD, AC = 4 and angle A = 30°, so CD = 4·sin30° = 2. In right triangle BCD, angle B = 45°, so it is a 45°-45°-90° triangle; with leg CD = 2, the hypotenuse BC = 2√2. Therefore a = 2√2.
